Kuvitus: huvipuiston vuoristorata kesäpä: Illustration: a roller coaster in an amusement park on a summer day. On the left rises the first and highest hill of the track, and a red train has just reached its top. After that the track descends into a deep valley and rises to a second hill, which is clearly lower, and then to a third hill that is lower still. There are white support columns under the track and a spruce forest in the background.
Kaavakuva, ei mittakaavassa: vuoristorad: Schematic diagram, not to scale: a roller coaster car in a curved valley without friction or air resistance. The car starts from rest on the left at a height h (point 1), passes half the height (point 2) and the bottom of the valley (point 3) and stops on the right at the same height h (point 4). The blue arrows are the velocity of the car, greatest at the bottom. Below, the energy bars of each point: green potential energy and blue kinetic energy. At points 1 and 4 there is only potential energy, at point 3 only kinetic energy, and at point 2 half of each. The sum of the bars is equal at every point.
Kaavakuva kolmesta tilanteesta, joissa l: Schematic diagram of three situations in which a box moves to the right on a floor; the blue arrow is the velocity of the box. On the left the box is pulled in the direction of the motion with a force F, so the force does positive work, W > 0. In the middle the frictional force F_μ from the surface of the floor acts against the motion, so it does negative work, W < 0. On the right the normal force N of the floor is perpendicular to the motion, so it does no work, W = 0.
Energiapalkit, kaavakuva mittakaavassa:: Energy bars, schematic diagram to scale: at the start the object has only potential energy E_p,1, and the kinetic energy E_k,1 is zero. Friction does the negative work W_other, whose bar points downward from the zero level. At the end the object has only kinetic energy E_k,2, and the potential energy E_p,2 is zero. The dashed line at the height of the initial mechanical energy shows that the final energy is smaller than the initial energy by exactly the work of friction.
